refuters.argument:
I attacked the three topological points and the surrounding clauses and found no place where the Lean statement is weaker than the printed one, adds a restrictive hypothesis, quantifies differently, or names a different object.

1. Continuity / topology on labelled tuples. Elaborating the reviewer statement file with `pp.explicit` (a copy in /tmp importing the compiled olean of SM.MyCyclicB; I did not open its source) shows `JoinedIn` on `LabelledTuple n` is taken at `@Pi.topologicalSpace (ZMod n) (fun _ => Plane) (fun _ => @instTopologicalSpaceProd ℝ ℝ (UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace ... Real.pseudoMetricSpace) (...))`, i.e. the product topology over the finite index set ZMod n of the product topology on ℝ×ℝ with the standard metric topology on ℝ — the Euclidean topology on (ℝ²)^n. A grep over all of work/lean/SM (the two forbidden files excluded) finds no other `TopologicalSpace` instance on `LabelledTuple`, `Plane`, `ZMod` or anything else (only `Classical.propDecidable` and one `NeZero` local instance), and no local redefinition of `JoinedIn`, `IsPathConnected` or `Path`. Mathlib: `JoinedIn F x y := ∃ γ : Path x y, ∀ t, γ t ∈ F`, `Path x y extends C(I, X)` with `source' : toFun 0 = x` and target 1 = y. So `JoinedIn {Q | Regular Q ∧ rotationNumber Q = r} P P'` is exactly "a continuous path in ℛ_n ∩ rot⁻¹(r) joins P to P'". `Regular` unfolds to ∀ i, edge P (i-1) ≠ 0 ∧ edge P i ≠ 0 ∧ ¬∃ r<0, edge P i = r • edge P (i-1) (printed def:regular verbatim), `rotationNumber P = (∑ principalTurn P i)/(2π)` with `principalTurn = arg(conj(ℓ_{i-1})·ℓ_i)` ∈ (−π,π) for regular pairs, cos = dot/(|u||v|), sign = sign det (printed def:regular/lem:rot).

2. Quotient topology on Polygon. The elaborated `orbit_fibre_pathConnected` uses `@instTopologicalSpaceQuotient (LabelledTuple n) (cyclicSetoid n) (Pi.topologicalSpace ...)`; Mathlib defines this as `coinduced Quotient.mk' t`, and I checked by `rfl` that it equals `TopologicalSpace.coinduced (@Quotient.mk' (LabelledTuple n) (cyclicSetoid n)) Pi.topologicalSpace` at type `TopologicalSpace (Polygon n hn)` (Polygon n hn := Quotient (cyclicSetoid n), a def, unfolds by delta). This is the quotient topology of (ℝ²)^n by ℤ/n — the only sensible reading of def:polygon's "the space of polygons is the quotient (ℝ²)^n/(ℤ/n)".

3. Orbits. `cyclicSetoid n` relates P Q iff `∃ k : ZMod n, Q = shift k P`, and `shift k P i = P (i + k)` (rfl), so `shift 1 = σ` in the printed direction `(σP)_i = μ_{i+1}` and `shift k = σ^k` via `shift_add`. I machine-checked `Quotient.mk (cyclicSetoid n) P = Quotient.mk (cyclicSetoid n) Q ↔ ∃ k, Q = shift k P`, so `⟦P⟧` is exactly the printed orbit `[P] = {σ^k P : k ∈ ℤ/n}`. The Lean set `{Q | ∃ P, Regular P ∧ rotationNumber P = r ∧ Q = Quotient.mk (cyclicSetoid n) P}` is the image of ℛ_n ∩ rot⁻¹(r) under the quotient map; since `regular_shift` and `rotationNumber_shift` (checked by rw) make both predicates shift-invariant, this coincides with the set of orbits all of whose representatives are regular of rotation r — both readings of "fibre of cyclic polygon orbits" agree.

4. Which fibre. The printed last sentence starts with "Thus", i.e. it is derived from sentences 1–2 about ℛ_n, and the proof's last sentence reads "Passing any constructed path to the cyclic quotient identifies its shifted target with the original target orbit, proving the orbit statement." The constructed paths live in ℛ_n ∩ rot⁻¹(r), so the printed theorem supports the ℛ_n reading, which the Lean set implements. The def:admissible object 𝒰_{n,r} (generic locus) is a different set whose quotient's path-connectedness does not follow from sentences 1–2 and is not what this theorem asserts.

5. Remaining clauses. `joined` carries the printed hypotheses (P, P' regular, rot = r) and the printed exclusion `((n:ℤ), r) ≠ (4,0)`; `joined_shift` has `∃ k : ZMod n` with n = 4 forced by the hypothesis, target `shift k P' = σ^k P'`. Sentence 3: `bowTie` is ((0,0),(2,2),(0,2),(2,0)) at labels 1,2,3,4≡0 (def:star); `bowTie_mem` (shifts in ℛ_4 ∩ rot⁻¹(0)), `bowTie_components` (joined in the fibre ↔ equal shift), `turn_word_constant` (turn word i ↦ turn Q i = χ_{i−1,i,i+1} constant along paths in the fibre) and `bowTie_turn_words` (the four words pairwise distinct) render "lie in the four distinct labelled components, distinguished by their turn words"; the proof text confirms "labelled components" are path components of the labelled fibre and the words are the turn-sign words, "There are exactly four components", which follows from the bundle at (4,0) (joined_shift with P' = K_0 plus bowTie_components). `Admissible (n:ℤ) r := 3 ≤ n ∧ 2|r| < n ∧ (n,r) ≠ (3,0)` is def:admissible verbatim.

Where Lean differs, it is only stronger or harmlessly typed: Mathlib's `IsPathConnected` includes nonemptiness (∃ x ∈ F, ...), so the last field additionally asserts every admissible fibre is nonempty (true, and a burden on the prover, not a weakening); `[NeZero n]` and `hn : 3 ≤ n` are both consequences of `Admissible (n:ℤ) r` (n ≥ 3), so they add no restriction. I found nothing to refute.
